Hi Sarah,
I apologize for this additional issue, but I wanted to confirm my
assessment before contacting you directly. This involves the BC04 rather
than the THOR P2; my BC04 was included in order number ····-A. I mentioned
this to Mike via Discord the gentleman who used to appear in videos with JD
but I noticed that when Helium deploys mails its products, it ships them
only in the box containing the miner, without an outer box for better
transport. My BC04 arrived in its box inside what I believe was an Amazon
bag. I will send photos, but essentially it was opened from the top; at
that time I hadn’t realized there is a seal at the bottom. (In the past
month I have purchased about 14 miners from different companies, so I have
been opening a lot of boxes. But I purchased another BC04 from Altair Tech,
and they ship their miners in their box but then put it in another box for
better transport. Anyway, as you see in the photos, my miner box came a
little more beat up and it was opened from the top.)

My concern is that I was comparing the Altair Tech shipped BC04 fan and the
Helium deploys BC04. If you look at the screenshot, when the Helium deploy
fan is at 100 percent it is only doing 2784 RPM, the chip is at 57.5 and
VRM at 71. But when you see the Altair Tech BC04 fan at 87 percent it is
doing 3517 RPM and is keeping the chip cooler along with the VRM chip at
51.4 and 57.3. You will also hear in the video how the Altair Tech BC04 is
louder and moving more air than the Helium deploy at 100 percent. I had
recently gotten the Altair BC04 so I was not able to compare until now.At
the time, I overlooked how the HD-shipped BC04 opened from the top, whereas
the Altair BC04 was unsealed from the bottom and opened upward. Tampering
might be possible, though I am unsure. Something is clearly wrong with the
fan’s operation. As I mentioned, I have ordered many miners and received a
lot of mail, so I should have paid closer attention to the box; initially
the HD BC04 seemed fine, but comparing them at the same specifications
shows something unusual with the HD unit. Although both use the same
firmware, the overclock settings display different frequency and core
voltage values; to ensure a fair comparison, I manually adjusted the HD
BC04 frequency to match the Altair, since overclock mode does not allow
changes.

Regardless, I recommend that HD ship products in the original miner box
plus an outer box for better protection perhaps that explains the odd noise
from the Thor’s PSU. My BC04 arrived only in the original box inside an
Amazon bag and opened from the top rather than the seal, suggesting
possible interference; the fan still performs poorly when compared directly
with the Altair unit. I apologize for being long-winded, but I would
appreciate assistance because the fan seems odd. Both units share the same
firmware number.
